title: Functions of Management

topics.title: Functions of Management
topics.description: The four primary functions of management are Planning, Organizing, Leading (Directing), and Controlling. Planning involves setting goals and determining the best way to achieve them. Organizing involves assigning tasks and allocating resources. Leading involves motivating and influencing employees to work toward goals. Controlling involves monitoring progress and making corrections.

topics.title: Levels of Management
topics.description: Management is typically divided into three levels: Top-level (strategic), Middle-level (tactical), and First-line (operational). Top managers focus on long-term goals and the organization as a whole. Middle managers translate top-level goals into specific plans for their departments. First-line managers oversee the daily activities of non-managerial employees.

topics.title: Leadership vs Management
topics.description: While the terms are often used interchangeably, they are distinct. Management is about process, stability, and control—doing things right. Leadership is about vision, inspiration, and change—doing the right things. Effective managers must also be leaders, but not all leaders are managers.

topics.title: Organizational Goals
topics.description: Goals provide direction and a sense of purpose. They can be strategic (long-term, broad), tactical (intermediate, specific), or operational (short-term, highly detailed). Goals should align throughout the organization to ensure everyone is working toward the same mission.

topics.title: Managerial Effectiveness
topics.description: Effectiveness is 'doing the right things'—the degree to which an organization achieves its goals. Efficiency is 'doing things right'—achieving goals with minimal waste of resources. High-performing managers balance both.

roleplayConnection: In FBLA Business Management role plays, judges look for a clear understanding of how management functions interact. If you are tasked with solving a problem in a department, you must explain how you will PLAN the solution, ORGANIZE the resources, LEAD the team through the change, and CONTROL the outcome through KPIs. Failing to mention all four can signal a lack of holistic management thinking.

mcqs.question: A CEO is developing a 10-year vision for the company's expansion into international markets. Which management function is primarily being exercised?
mcqs.explanation: Planning involves setting long-term goals and determining the strategies to achieve them. A 10-year vision is a strategic plan.

mcqs.question: Which level of management is typically responsible for translating broad strategic goals into specific tactical objectives?
mcqs.explanation: Middle managers act as the bridge between top-level strategy and first-line operations, developing tactical plans.

mcqs.question: A manager notice that the production line is producing 10% more waste than the standard allowed. They initiate a meeting to find the root cause. This is an example of:
mcqs.explanation: Controlling involves monitoring performance, comparing it against standards, and taking corrective action.

mcqs.question: According to Peter Drucker, 'doing things right' refers to ________, while 'doing the right things' refers to ________.
mcqs.explanation: Efficiency is doing things right (optimizing resources), while effectiveness is doing the right things (achieving goals).

mcqs.question: Which of the following skills becomes MORE important as a manager moves up to higher levels of the organization?
mcqs.explanation: Conceptual skills—the ability to see the organization as a whole and the relationship between its parts—are critical for top-level strategic management.

mcqs.question: An operational manager spends most of their time:
mcqs.explanation: First-line or operational managers work directly with the employees who produce the products or services.

mcqs.question: Which management function involves determining what tasks are to be done, who is to do them, and how the tasks are to be grouped?
mcqs.explanation: Organizing is the process of structuring the workforce and resources to carry out the plans.

mcqs.question: A manager who inspires their team to achieve a difficult goal during a crisis is primarily demonstrating:
mcqs.explanation: Leading (or Directing) involves motivating, influencing, and guiding employees toward goal achievement.

mcqs.question: Strategic goals are typically:
mcqs.explanation: Strategic goals set the long-term direction (usually 3-5+ years) for the entire organization.

mcqs.question: The 'Chain of Command' refers to:
options: The total number of employees in a company
The continuous line of authority that connects everyone in the organization
The list of rules in the employee handbook
mcqs.explanation: The chain of command is the hierarchy of authority that dictates who reports to whom.

mcqs.question: When a manager is performing the 'Interpersonal' role as defined by Mintzberg, they are acting as a:
mcqs.explanation: The figurehead role is one of Mintzberg's interpersonal roles, involving symbolic legal or social duties.

mcqs.question: Which of these is a 'Decisional' role according to Mintzberg?
mcqs.explanation: Entrepreneur is a decisional role where the manager seeks to improve the unit by initiating projects.

mcqs.question: A company decides to outsource its payroll function to save money. This is primarily a decision regarding:
mcqs.explanation: Outsourcing for cost savings is an effort to improve efficiency (reducing resource usage).

mcqs.question: The 'Double-Loop Learning' concept in management refers to:
options: Checking if a task was done correctly
Changing the goals based on results
Correcting errors and then questioning the underlying values/policies
mcqs.explanation: Double-loop learning involves questioning the assumptions and policies that led to an error, rather than just fixing the error.

mcqs.question: Which management scholar is known for the '14 Principles of Management'?
mcqs.explanation: Henri Fayol developed the 14 principles of management, which are foundational to modern organizational theory.

mcqs.question: Total Quality Management (TQM) is most closely related to which management function?
mcqs.explanation: TQM is a continuous process of detecting and reducing or eliminating errors, which is a core part of the controlling function.

mcqs.question: Span of control refers to:
options: The number of employees a manager can efficiently and effectively lead
The duration of a manager's contract
mcqs.explanation: Span of control defines how many subordinates report directly to one manager.

mcqs.question: A matrix organizational structure violates which of Fayol's principles?
mcqs.explanation: Unity of command states an employee should have only one superior. In a matrix, they often report to both a functional and a project manager.

mcqs.question: The 'Hawthorne Studies' concluded that:
options: Employee performance improves when they feel observed and valued
Higher pay is the only motivator
mcqs.explanation: The Hawthorne Effect suggests that social factors and being singled out for attention can increase productivity.

mcqs.question: Management by Objectives (MBO) is a process where:
options: Managers and employees jointly set goals and review progress
Goals are set by an external consultant
mcqs.explanation: MBO involves a collaborative process of goal setting to ensure alignment and motivation.

title: Strategic Planning & Analysis

topics.title: Strategic Planning
topics.description: Strategic planning is the process of defining an organization's strategy, or direction, and making decisions on allocating its resources to pursue this strategy. It typically involves a 3-5 year horizon.

topics.title: Tactical & Operational Planning
topics.description: Tactical planning (6 months - 2 years) breaks down strategic goals into specific actions for departments. Operational planning (daily/weekly) focuses on the execution of specific tasks.

topics.title: SWOT Analysis
topics.description: A framework used to evaluate a company's competitive position. Strengths and Weaknesses are internal factors. Opportunities and Threats are external factors.

topics.title: SMART Goals
topics.description: Goals should be Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. This framework ensures goals are clear and trackable.

topics.title: PESTEL Analysis
topics.description: Analyzes the macro-environment: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Environmental, and Legal factors.

roleplayConnection: Judges in strategic roles will ask you to justify a new initiative. You should use a SWOT analysis to frame your answer. For example, 'This expansion leverages our STRENGTH in brand loyalty while mitigating the THREAT of a new competitor.' This shows you aren't just guessing, but using industry-standard tools to make decisions.

mcqs.question: In a SWOT analysis, a rising interest rate in the economy would be classified as a:
mcqs.explanation: Economic factors like interest rates are external to the firm and usually represent a threat (if rising costs of borrowing) or opportunity.

mcqs.question: Which type of planning involves daily work schedules and specific task assignments?
mcqs.explanation: Operational planning deals with the day-to-day activities of the organization.

mcqs.question: A 'Mission Statement' typically answers which question?
options: What do we want to become in 20 years?
What is our reason for being today?
What are our specific profit targets for this year?
How do we beat our top competitor?
mcqs.explanation: A mission statement defines the company's core purpose and current business focus.

mcqs.question: A 'Vision Statement' is primarily:
mcqs.explanation: A vision statement describes what the organization hopes to become in the future.

mcqs.question: The 'M' in SMART goals stands for:
mcqs.explanation: Measurable means there is a clear metric to track progress toward the goal.

mcqs.question: Which of Michael Porter's Generic Strategies involves targeting a narrow market segment with a low-cost approach?
mcqs.explanation: Cost Focus targets a specific niche with a cost-advantaged strategy.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of an internal factor in a SWOT analysis?
mcqs.explanation: Proprietary technology is an internal strength of the organization.

mcqs.question: Contingency planning is best described as:
options: A plan for when things go wrong ('Plan B')
A plan for the best-case scenario
mcqs.explanation: Contingency planning involves developing alternative courses of action for unexpected events.

mcqs.question: Which step comes first in the strategic management process?
mcqs.explanation: Environmental scanning (internal and external analysis) is the foundation of the strategic process.

mcqs.question: A company decides to focus on 'Differentiation' as its primary strategy. What is its main goal?
options: To have the lowest prices in the market
To offer unique products that consumers perceive as more valuable
To target only one specific city
mcqs.explanation: Differentiation aims to create unique value for which customers are willing to pay a premium.

mcqs.question: The 'Boston Consulting Group (BCG) Matrix' classifies products based on:
mcqs.explanation: The BCG Matrix uses market growth rate and relative market share to categorize business units (Stars, Cash Cows, Dogs, Question Marks).

mcqs.question: A 'Cash Cow' in the BCG Matrix is characterized by:
mcqs.explanation: Cash Cows generate more cash than they consume, typically in mature, low-growth markets where they have high share.

mcqs.question: Benchmarking is the process of:
options: Comparing your business processes and performance metrics to industry best practices
mcqs.explanation: Benchmarking involves looking outside the firm to find superior methods and adopting them.

mcqs.question: Which of Porter's Five Forces deals with how easily customers can switch to a competitor?
mcqs.explanation: The power of buyers increases when they have many choices and low switching costs.

mcqs.question: A 'Barriers to Entry' example in the Five Forces model would be:
mcqs.explanation: High capital requirements make it difficult for new competitors to enter the market.

mcqs.question: Scenario planning differs from traditional forecasting because:
options: It considers multiple possible futures rather than one single prediction
It only looks at the past
It is done by lower-level employees
mcqs.explanation: Scenario planning prepares managers for different potential environments.

mcqs.question: The 'Experience Curve' suggests that:
options: Costs decrease as cumulative volume of production increases
mcqs.explanation: As a company gains experience producing a product, it finds ways to reduce costs.

mcqs.question: Vertical Integration involves:
options: Gaining control over suppliers or distributors
mcqs.explanation: Vertical integration can be backward (suppliers) or forward (distributors).

mcqs.question: A 'Core Competency' is defined as:
options: A unique strength that is difficult for competitors to copy
The ability to use Microsoft Excel
The minimum requirement to stay in business
mcqs.explanation: Core competencies provide a sustainable competitive advantage.

mcqs.question: Strategy implementation is often called the ________ stage of management.
mcqs.explanation: Implementation is the execution phase where plans are put into action.

title: Organizational Structure & Design

topics.title: Organizational Structures
topics.description: Common structures include Functional (by department), Divisional (by product/region), Matrix (dual reporting), and Flat (minimal levels). The choice depends on size, strategy, and environment.

topics.title: Delegation
topics.description: The assignment of authority to another person to carry out specific activities. It involves Responsibility (the obligation), Authority (the right), and Accountability (the answerability).

topics.title: Centralization vs Decentralization
topics.description: Centralization is when decision-making authority is concentrated at the top. Decentralization pushes authority down to lower levels. Trends favor decentralization for faster response times.

topics.title: Chain of Command
topics.description: The line of authority extending from upper levels to the lowest levels, clarifying who reports to whom. Modern organizations are shortening this chain.

topics.title: Formalization
topics.description: The degree to which jobs within the organization are standardized and the extent to which employee behavior is guided by rules and procedures.

roleplayConnection: In role plays involving organizational change, you might need to suggest a change in structure. If a company is growing too fast and the CEO is overwhelmed, suggest DECENTRALIZATION or a DIVISIONAL structure. Explain how this reduces the CEO's 'Span of Control' and empowers local managers to make faster decisions.

mcqs.question: Which organizational structure groups employees based on their skills and expertise (e.g., Marketing, Finance, HR)?
mcqs.explanation: A functional structure is based on the specialized activities of the business.

mcqs.question: In a Matrix structure, an employee usually reports to:
mcqs.explanation: Matrix structures involve reporting to both a functional manager and a project/product manager.

mcqs.question: Authority is defined as:
options: The obligation to perform a task
The right to give orders and expect them to be obeyed
The ability to influence others without formal power
The total number of years worked
mcqs.explanation: Authority is the formal power granted by the organization.

mcqs.question: Accountability means that a person is:
options: Answerable for the results of a task
In charge of the accounting department
mcqs.explanation: While responsibility can be delegated, ultimate accountability usually remains with the delegator or is shared.

mcqs.question: A 'Flat' organization is characterized by:
options: Few or no levels of management
mcqs.explanation: Flat organizations have a wide span of control and fewer management layers.

mcqs.question: Which factor would favor a CENTRALIZED decision-making structure?
options: Managers are highly skilled and want autonomy
mcqs.explanation: Centralization is more effective in stable environments where top-level control is efficient.

mcqs.question: The 'Scalar Principle' refers to:
options: The need for a clear, unbroken line of authority from top to bottom
The process of scaling a business
mcqs.explanation: This is another name for the Scalar Chain or Chain of Command.

mcqs.question: Which type of structure is organized around specific geographic areas or customer groups?
mcqs.explanation: Divisional structures can be based on products, geography, or customers.

mcqs.question: Formalization is likely to be HIGHEST in which type of organization?
mcqs.explanation: Bureaucracies and large government entities rely heavily on standardized rules and procedures.

mcqs.question: Span of Management is also known as:
mcqs.explanation: These terms are used interchangeably to describe how many subordinates report to a manager.

mcqs.question: Which of these is a disadvantage of a FUNCTIONAL structure?
mcqs.explanation: Functional departments can become isolated and fail to see the big picture.

mcqs.question: A 'Virtual' organization is one that:
options: Only exists in a video game
Outsources most of its major business functions
mcqs.explanation: A virtual (or network) organization maintains a small core and contracts out everything else.

mcqs.question: When a manager delegates a task, they also delegate:
mcqs.explanation: Responsibility is given to the subordinate, but the manager remains accountable.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of 'Staff' authority?
options: A sales manager telling a salesperson to make more calls
An HR manager advising a production manager on hiring laws
mcqs.explanation: Staff authority is advisory and supportive, whereas line authority is the direct right to command.

mcqs.question: Mechanistic organizations are characterized by:
mcqs.explanation: Mechanistic structures are rigid and bureaucratic, suitable for stable environments.

mcqs.question: Organic organizations are best suited for:
mcqs.explanation: Organic structures are flexible and adaptable, often found in high-tech or creative industries.

mcqs.question: Work Specialization is also known as:
mcqs.explanation: This involves breaking down tasks into small, repetitive steps.

mcqs.question: The primary goal of a Matrix structure is to:
options: Balance functional expertise with project-specific needs
mcqs.explanation: Matrix structures aim to get the best of both functional and divisional worlds.

mcqs.question: A 'Tall' organizational structure has:
options: Narrow spans of control and many levels
Wide spans of control and few levels
mcqs.explanation: Tall hierarchies have many layers, which can slow down communication.

mcqs.question: Bureaucracy, as described by Max Weber, is based on:
mcqs.explanation: Weber's model of bureaucracy emphasizes logic, order, and legitimate authority.

title: Human Resource Management

topics.title: Staffing & Workforce Planning
topics.description: The process of determining the number and types of employees needed and ensuring they are in the right place at the right time. It starts with job analysis.

topics.title: Recruiting & Hiring
topics.description: Recruiting is attracting a pool of qualified candidates. Hiring involves selecting the best candidate through interviews, tests, and background checks.

topics.title: Employee Onboarding
topics.description: The process of integrating new employees into the organization and its culture, providing them with the tools and information needed to succeed.

topics.title: Performance Evaluation
topics.description: The systematic assessment of an employee's performance based on predetermined standards. Methods include 360-degree feedback, MBO, and graphic rating scales.

topics.title: Compensation & Benefits
topics.description: The total reward package given to employees, including base pay, incentives (bonuses), and benefits (insurance, 401k).

roleplayConnection: HR role plays often focus on solving low morale or high turnover. You must address the ROOT CAUSE. If turnover is high, look at the STAFFING process—are we hiring the wrong people? Or is the PERFORMANCE EVALUATION unfair? Propose a solution like 'Implementing 360-degree feedback' to increase transparency and fairness.

mcqs.question: What is the first step in the HR planning process?
mcqs.explanation: Job analysis (determining the duties and requirements of a job) is foundational to all HR activities.

mcqs.question: A 'Job Description' focuses on ________, while a 'Job Specification' focuses on ________.
mcqs.explanation: Description = what the job is. Specification = what the person needs (skills, degree, etc.).

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an ADVANTAGE of internal recruiting?
options: Provides a larger pool of candidates
mcqs.explanation: Internal candidates already know the culture and processes.

mcqs.question: An 'Orientation' program for new hires is primarily designed to:
options: Reduce initial anxiety and socialize the employee
mcqs.explanation: Orientation (or onboarding) helps new employees transition into the company.

mcqs.question: Which performance appraisal method involves getting feedback from subordinates, peers, and supervisors?
mcqs.explanation: 360-degree feedback provides a well-rounded view of performance.

mcqs.question: The 'Halo Effect' in interviewing occurs when:
options: One positive characteristic causes the interviewer to overlook negative ones
The interview is conducted in a church
mcqs.explanation: This is a common bias where a single trait colors the entire evaluation.

mcqs.question: Which law prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin?
options: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act
mcqs.explanation: Title VII (1964) is the primary anti-discrimination law in employment.

mcqs.question: The 'Fair Labor Standards Act' (FLSA) primarily regulates:
mcqs.explanation: FLSA established the minimum wage and the 40-hour work week.

mcqs.question: A 'Structured Interview' is one where:
options: The interviewer asks the same set of predetermined questions to all candidates
The interview happens at a construction site
mcqs.explanation: Structured interviews increase fairness and allow for better comparison between candidates.

mcqs.question: What is 'Attrition'?
options: The process of hiring new people
The natural reduction of the workforce through retirement or resignation
The act of firing an employee
mcqs.explanation: Attrition happens when people leave and are not immediately replaced.

mcqs.question: Which type of training happens while the employee is performing their actual job duties?
mcqs.explanation: OJT is the most common form of training, happening in the work environment.

mcqs.question: Collective Bargaining is a process between:
mcqs.explanation: Collective bargaining determines contract terms for unionized workers.

mcqs.question: Which of these is a 'Non-exempt' employee under the FLSA?
options: An employee entitled to overtime pay
mcqs.explanation: Non-exempt employees must be paid overtime (1.5x) for hours worked over 40.

mcqs.question: A 'Skilled-based' pay system rewards employees for:
options: The number of hours they work
The variety and depth of skills they possess
mcqs.explanation: This encourages employees to learn more and become more versatile.

mcqs.question: What is 'Glass Ceiling'?
options: An invisible barrier that prevents women and minorities from reaching top management
The limit on how much an employee can be paid
mcqs.explanation: It refers to the subtle, often systemic barriers to advancement.

mcqs.question: Adverse Impact occurs when:
options: An employment practice that appears neutral has a discriminatory effect on a protected group
mcqs.explanation: This is also known as 'disparate impact' and is illegal under civil rights laws.

mcqs.question: Which of these is a MANDATORY benefit in the US?
mcqs.explanation: Social Security and workers' compensation are mandatory; many others are voluntary or regulated by firm size.

mcqs.question: What is the purpose of a 'Probationary Period'?
options: To evaluate a new hire's fit and performance before making the position permanent
To train them for a different job
mcqs.explanation: Typically 90 days, this allows both parties to see if the match is right.

mcqs.question: Hostile Work Environment is a type of:
mcqs.explanation: It involves unwelcome conduct that makes the workplace intimidating or offensive.

mcqs.question: Human Capital refers to:
options: The value of the employees' skills, knowledge, and experience
mcqs.explanation: People are considered an asset with measurable value.

title: Leadership & Motivation

topics.title: Leadership Styles
topics.description: Common styles include Autocratic (leader decides), Democratic (group decides), and Laissez-faire (leader is hands-off). Modern theories include Transformational (vision-based) and Situational leadership.

topics.title: Motivation Theories
topics.description: Includes Maslow's Hierarchy (needs), Herzberg's Two-Factor (hygiene vs. motivators), and Vroom's Expectancy theory. Understanding what drives people is key to management.

topics.title: Communication Methods
topics.description: Effective communication involves the sender, message, channel, receiver, and feedback. Barriers include noise, selective perception, and emotional disconnects.

topics.title: Team Management
topics.description: Teams go through stages: Forming, Storming, Norming, Performing, and Adjourning (Tuckman's Model). Managers must guide the team through these stages.

topics.title: Conflict Resolution
topics.description: Techniques include Competing, Collaborating, Avoiding, Accommodating, and Compromising. The goal is often win-win solutions.

roleplayConnection: Leadership role plays often put you in a 'Conflict' scenario. Use the SITUATIONAL leadership model in your answer. Say, 'Because the employees are highly skilled but lack motivation, I will use a PARTICIPATIVE style to involve them in decision-making and rebuild their commitment.' This proves you can adapt your style to the specific needs of the team.

mcqs.question: Which leadership style involves the leader making all decisions without consulting subordinates?
mcqs.explanation: Autocratic (or authoritarian) leaders retain all power and decision-making authority.

mcqs.question: According to Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs, which need is at the VERY bottom (most basic)?
mcqs.explanation: Physiological needs (food, water, shelter) must be met before any other needs.

mcqs.question: In Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory, which of the following is a 'Hygiene' factor?
mcqs.explanation: Hygiene factors (like pay and conditions) don't motivate if present, but cause dissatisfaction if missing.

mcqs.question: Transformational leaders are known for:
options: Inspiring followers to transcend self-interest for the good of the organization
mcqs.explanation: Transformational leadership is about vision and large-scale change.

mcqs.question: Tuckman's model of team development starts with which stage?
mcqs.explanation: Forming is the initial stage where team members get to know each other.

mcqs.question: Expectancy Theory suggests that motivation depends on:
options: The belief that effort leads to performance, and performance leads to a desired reward
mcqs.explanation: Vroom's theory focuses on the mental process regarding choice and rewards.

mcqs.question: Which communication barrier involves the receiver hearing only what they want to hear based on their own needs and experience?
mcqs.explanation: Selective perception filters information through a personal lens.

mcqs.question: A 'Laissez-faire' leader:
options: Provides little or no direction and gives followers as much freedom as possible
mcqs.explanation: This 'let it be' style works well with highly skilled, self-motivated teams.

mcqs.question: According to McGregor, 'Theory X' managers believe that employees:
options: Dislike work and must be coerced to perform
mcqs.explanation: Theory X is a pessimistic view of human nature.

mcqs.question: Equity Theory focuses on:
options: How much money the company has
The fairness of the rewards received compared to the efforts and rewards of others
Giving everyone exactly the same pay
mcqs.explanation: Employees compare their input/output ratio to that of 'referent' others.

mcqs.question: Which conflict resolution style involves both parties giving up something to reach a solution?
mcqs.explanation: Compromise is a middle-ground where no one wins entirely but progress is made.

mcqs.question: Non-verbal communication includes:
mcqs.explanation: Non-verbal cues often convey more meaning than words themselves.

mcqs.question: A 'Servant Leader' focuses primarily on:
options: The growth and well-being of people and the communities to which they belong
mcqs.explanation: Servant leadership prioritizes the needs of others.

mcqs.question: Groupthink is a phenomenon where:
options: Groups make better decisions than individuals
The desire for harmony in a group results in irrational or dysfunctional decision-making
The group uses computers to think
mcqs.explanation: Groupthink discourages dissenting opinions and critical thinking.

mcqs.question: Intrinsic motivation comes from:
options: Personal satisfaction and interest in the work itself
mcqs.explanation: Intrinsic motivation is internal to the individual.

mcqs.question: Which of these is an example of an EXTRINSIC reward?
mcqs.explanation: Extrinsic rewards are external (tangible) rewards given by others.

mcqs.question: Active Listening involves:
options: Thinking about your response while the other person talks
Providing verbal and non-verbal feedback to show full engagement
mcqs.explanation: Active listening requires effort to truly understand the sender's message.

mcqs.question: The 'Grapevine' in an organization is:
mcqs.explanation: Informal communication is fast but can be prone to rumors.

mcqs.question: Which leadership theory suggests that there is no 'one best way' to lead and that the style should depend on the situation?
mcqs.explanation: Fiedler's Contingency Model and Hersey-Blanchard Situational Leadership are key examples.

mcqs.question: Social Loafing is the tendency for individuals to:
options: Put in less effort when working in a group compared to working alone
mcqs.explanation: Social loafing occurs when individual accountability is low in a group setting.

topics.title: Compensation
topics.description: Direct and indirect rewards for labor.

topics.title: Retention

topics.title: Scope management

topics.title: Knowledge management
